query: For a multicomponent high-entropy alloy in its high-temperature solid and liquid states, what single intervention could overcome the limited accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties across a large compositional space? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention and causal mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to current experimental and computational baselines, defines the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive falsification test against independent reference data.

revised_generation.hypothesis: Intervention of machine learning models can improve the accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties across a large compositional space for high-entropy alloys.
revised_generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys in their high-temperature solid and liquid states.
revised_generation.mechanism: Improved accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties.
revised_generation.predicted_outcome: Improved accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties.
revised_generation.boundary: High-entropy alloys in their high-temperature solid and liquid states.
revised_generation.uncertainty: Limited availability of thermodynamic data and potential uncertainty in machine learning model accuracy.

In Situ Heating STEM Investigations

AuCoCuNiPt NPs were fabricated by Pulsed Laser Deposition (PLD) directly on the amorphous 50 nm thick SiN film of a heating TEM microchip ( Figure 1 a , see Experimental Section). [ [2] ] Particle diameter in the as‐prepared sample ranges from 3–6.5 nm with a mean diameter of 4.5 nm (Figure 1b ). Prior to heating, the composition of individual NPs was measured by energy dispersive X‐ray spectroscopy (EDS) in STEM mode (Figure S1 , Supporting Information). The spider plot in Figure 1c shows that particle composition is uniform and ≈Au 20 Co 28 Cu 11 Ni 20 Pt 21 with a dispersion below 5%. EDS chemical maps revealed the homogenous distribution of the five metals in the NPs (Figure S2a , Supporting Information), and the Face Centered Cubic (FCC) structure of NPs assembly was confirmed by electron diffraction (Figure S2b , Supporting Information). High‐resolution imaging was exploited to identify the various shapes of as‐grown NPs. To improve data quality, NPs fabricated on 5 nm‐thick carbon film were also analyzed but the shape and structure of HENA are similar on both substrates (Figure S2 , Supporting Information).
